name: Payment webhook signature compared with insecure operator
attack_scenario: A non-constant-time or type-juggling comparison lets an attacker brute-force the signature byte-by-byte via response timing, or (in PHP loose comparison) submit a crafted `0e...` hash that compares equal, forging a valid payment-success callback and marking unpaid orders as paid.
negative_test_hint: submit a webhook whose razorpay_signature is "0e462097431906509019562988736854" and assert it is rejected by a constant-time comparison, never type-juggled or prefix-matched into equality

exemplar.explanation: Razorpay/PayU/PhonePe webhook-verification docs require a constant-time compare (timingSafeEqual / hash_equals / MessageDigest.isEqual). A plain == or .equals() on payment signatures leaks matching-prefix information through response timing (CWE-208), and in PHP loose comparison a crafted '0e...' magic hash type-juggles to equal (CWE-697) — both let an attacker forge payment-success callbacks and mark unpaid orders as paid.
